Our story

Baked for Bonnie.

Christina King learned these recipes at her mother’s counter — Bonnie Jacobs, who taught her cinnamon rolls and dinner rolls while Christina was raising toddler twins. It started with Christmas mornings.

In 2019 came a brain-cancer diagnosis, and with it, relearning to walk. Her physical therapists kept pushing her back toward the thing she loved — baking. Farmers markets came first, then the Buckley Kitchen in 2021, then Puyallup, and in December 2023 she and her husband Kenny opened the doors on Highway 410.

Christina can’t eat sugar. She bakes rolls she’ll never taste — and lets your first bite be the judge.

“It’s got to be fresh. I want that first bite that y’all have to speak: ‘I am home.’”

— Christina King, to the Courier-Herald
